pattern.crimePattern: a housekeeper the guard dogs know kills her employer to stop him reporting her brother for stock theft
pattern.notes: Fictional families, market staff and compound. Teaches the absence mechanic plainly: every expectation on the Expected list is grounded in a neighbour's or a son's statement.

ob.text: A woman delivering milk reports a livestock trader, Hussein Adan Ibrahim (52), found dead in the yard of his walled compound in Bula Pesa, Isiolo. The main gate was bolted from inside; she saw him through the gap under it.

facts.text: Hussein Adan Ibrahim was found dead in the yard of his compound in Bula Pesa on Friday morning; the main gate was bolted from inside.
He lay in the yard by the house door with one heavy blow to the side of the head.
His heavy hardwood herding stick lay beside him. There is not a single fingerprint on it.
Yasin: his father carried the stick everywhere, and Kaltuma moved it every day to sweep.
The main gate is bolted from inside; the back door to the lane has a spring latch that locks when pulled shut from outside.
Mama Safiya: every car that stops at Hussein's gate leaves tracks in the soft sand.
The broken glass along the wall top is intact, and the dust on it undisturbed.
The dogs' bowls hold fresh ugali and meat scraps, barely touched.
Hussein's cash drawer: KSh 47,000, untouched.
The concrete base of the water tank is clean: no blood, no mark.
Mama Safiya: "Those dogs bark at the bread boy every morning at five. They bark at me. They barked at the milk woman this morning. Last night: nothing. Not once."
Mama Safiya: Kaltuma feeds the dogs at half past five, chains them and goes home; the bowls are always licked clean by dark.
Mama Safiya: last week Mohamed Dahir shouted at Hussein in the street over a truck of goats.
Yasin: he argued with his father last week, on the phone, about his fees.
Yasin: only his father and Kaltuma have gate keys.
Market register, Saturday: 30 goats with Hussein's ear-notch, sold for KSh 165,000 by "Hassan Roba"; the herder who brought them was Jillo Wako.
Godana: he told Hussein on Wednesday. "He went quiet. He said, 'The boy has eaten my trust.' He said Friday, the police."
Godana was at home with his family on Thursday evening; he has no key to the compound, and the dogs bark at him.
Jillo's notebook: "Owed — 160,000 — pay by Sat."
Two herders: Jillo was at the grazing camp 12 km out all Thursday night.
Wario Bonaya: at about 21:05 on Thursday he took a young woman in a purple shawl from Wabera to Bula Pesa, and dropped her in the lane behind the compounds.
At Kaltuma's home: a purple shawl, freshly washed, on the line at 07:30 on Friday.
Records, Kaltuma's line: the Isiolo mast covers the whole town; on Thursday at 21:42, a 9-minute call to Jillo.
Modogashe checkpoint: Mohamed Dahir's lorry logged at 20:55 on Thursday, heading for Garissa.
Hostel register and bus ticket: Yasin has been in Nairobi since Monday.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy, rounded wooden object.
Post-mortem: death between 21:00 and 22:30 on Thursday.
Post-mortem: no stab wounds, no poison, no other injury.
Lab: purple wool fibres caught in the stick's split grip match Kaltuma's shawl.
Missing: the dogs didn't bark last night. Not once.
Missing: the bowls weren't licked clean. The dogs were fed again, after dark.
Missing: there are no climbing marks on the wall.
Missing: there are no fingerprints on the stick. It was wiped.
Missing: nothing was stolen.
Missing: there are no tyre tracks at the gate.
Kaltuma: "I fed the dogs at half past five and went home. I was home all night."
Kaltuma: she went back at night to beg for Jillo. "The dogs know me. I fed them so they'd be quiet." He said Friday, the police.
Kaltuma: "I don't remember picking up the stick. I never touched it."
Jillo: "I never sold the boss's goats."
Jillo: he sold them to pay men who don't wait. His sister called him at night crying, "It's finished." He thought she meant his job.
Dahir: "We fought over a truck. I was on the Garissa road."
Yasin: "I was in Nairobi. Father argued with everyone about money. He never hurt anyone."
Yasin: Kaltuma was paid to the end of the month, as always.

interrogations.intro: Kaltuma sits on a stool in Mama Safiya's kitchen, the purple shawl gone from her shoulders. "I fed the dogs at half past five and went home. I was home all night."
Jillo stands at the camp fence with his staff. "I never sold the boss's goats."
Dahir answers from Garissa, shouting over a lorry engine. "We fought over a truck. I was on the Garissa road."
Yasin calls from the Nairobi bus stage, crying. "I was in Nairobi. Father argued with everyone about money. He never hurt anyone."

topics.reply: "Father carried it everywhere. Kaltuma moved it every day to sweep. Only he and Kaltuma have gate keys."

interrogations.intro: Godana opens his register on the counting-office table.
Mama Safiya leans out of her kitchen window. "Those dogs. Let me tell you about those dogs."

contradictions.reaction: "I sold them. I owed money to men who don't wait. My sister called me at night crying and said 'it's finished'. I thought she meant my job."
She pulls her hands into her sleeves. "I went back to beg for Jillo. The dogs know me. I fed them so they'd be quiet. He said Friday, the police."
Kaltuma looks at the purple thread in the evidence bag for a long time. "He said Friday," she says again, very quietly.

reconstruction.text: Saturday. Jillo sells 30 of Hussein's goats at the Isiolo market under a friend's name, to pay a debt he is ashamed of.
Wednesday. Godana mentions the ear-notched goats. Hussein tells Jillo he will hand him to the police on Friday morning.
Thursday, 17:30. Kaltuma feeds the dogs, chains them and goes home as always.

21:05. A boda drops her in the lane. She lets herself in, feeds the dogs again so they stay quiet, and begs Hussein in the yard to forgive Jillo. "Friday. The police." As he turns away she picks up his herding stick.
She wipes the stick, bolts the gate from inside, and leaves by the back door on its spring latch. At 21:42 she calls Jillo, crying: "It's finished."

clockPlan.note: One stamp: records on Kaltuma. Detain her at her home; the fibres take 12 h plus 4 h transport, back at detention hour 16.

ui.beatNotes: The Expected list and the dotted card. At the dogs' corner the notebook shows expectations from Mama Safiya's statement: the dogs bark at strangers (absent last night), the bowls are licked clean by dark (absent), the dogs are chained at night (present). The player taps "note as missing"; a dotted card drops onto the board with a soft paper sound.
